title: The complete Crouzeix inequality
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's theorem (2026) that ||P[A]|| <= 2 max over the numerical range W(A) of ||P(z)|| for every complex square matrix A and every polynomial P with matrix coefficients of any size, with the sharp constant 2; this is the complete form of Crouzeix's conjecture. Convex domains with analytic polar boundaries approximate W(A) from outside; the Riemann map of the inverted exterior extends across the boundary; the Faber polynomials of the domain give a nonnegative kernel with marginals one and a two-sided estimate of boundary norms by coefficients; the resolvent q(lambda)(h(lambda)I - A)^(-1) has positive Hermitian part on the circle; testing it with the singular vectors of F[A] and the products FG and GF in both orders gives the constant 2.
prerequisites: linear algebra over C: tensor products of matrices, Hermitian and positive semidefinite matrices, the Hilbert-Schmidt norm, singular vectors

complex analysis as in the core course Complex Analysis (Lebl's Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis, cited by number at each use): Cauchy's integral formula and estimates, Laurent series, the residue theorem, Rouche's theorem, the open mapping theorem, the Riemann mapping theorem, harmonic conjugates and the reflection principle for harmonic functions

checks.reading: The manuscript 'A direct proof of the complete Crouzeix inequality' (OpenAI, 26 Sep 2026; build/main.tex, 622 lines, 36 kB of TeX, with its figures and references; local library copy openai-math-20261006) was read in full on 17 Oct 2026, and every step was derived again while the lessons were written. No error was found. Changes of form in the course: (1) the exterior coordinate (the manuscript's appendix) is constructed without Caratheodory's theorem on Jordan domains: the inverse Riemann map is extended across the boundary first, in boundary charts given by the analytic polar parametrization, by the reflection principle for harmonic functions applied to log|phi o Gamma| and a harmonic conjugate; the derivative is nonzero on the boundary by a sign argument on the lowest-order term; continuity of the Riemann map on the closed disc and its injectivity on the boundary follow from the local inverses; the boundary-chart, extension and patching results are stated for any bounded domain star-shaped about 0 with analytic polar boundary; (2) the analytic polar boundary of the outer approximations is proved with Rouche's theorem, the residue theorem and Morera's theorem (a holomorphic implicit function in one variable); (3) the joint expansion of s(lambda, mu) uses a lemma on continuous, separately holomorphic functions on a bidisc proved by iterated Cauchy integrals, so no several-variable theory is needed; (4) the Faber polynomials are given by an explicit recursion, and the identification of the Taylor coefficients of the resolvent with b_k(A) uses the same recursion; (5) the supporting line at a boundary point is obtained by a nearest-point argument and identified with the direction of q(lambda) by first-order conditions along the circle and along the radius; (6) the exercises add the uniqueness of the exterior map, the ellipse (Chebyshev polynomials, the Poisson kernel), Beckermann's bound ||b_k(A)|| <= 2 and its version for linear combinations. Follow-up literature on 17 Oct 2026 (arXiv searches for Crouzeix and for numerical range with spectral, sorted by date): no later work on the complete inequality was found; Crouzeix and Greenbaum, arXiv:2609.22460 (spectral constants of other regions from the scalar theorem), cited in the first lesson; Badea, O'Loughlin and Virtanen, arXiv:2609.03637 (the Clouatre-Ostermann-Ransford conjecture). The attribution of the case of order 2 to Badea, Crouzeix and Delyon was checked in the TeX source of Ahag, Czyz and Virtanen (arXiv:2608.27346v4, Section 1).
